meta.scope: Paraguay batch 3 — Asunción metro, departmental poverty contrast, MERCOSUR & trade agreements, education/health presence, and fiscal anchors. Completes the homogeneity check.
meta.homogeneity_note: Same national EPHC framework. Northern/interior departments (Concepción, San Pedro, Caazapá) carry the highest poverty; Asunción and Central are among the lowest. Large urban–rural gap, especially in extreme poverty.

candidates.title: Asunción — capital statistical identity
candidates.description: Capital city and primary urban economy. Core domain for EPHC labour, income and poverty analysis. Lowest departmental poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Dominant metro node. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain. 2025 total monetary poverty ~6.0% — the lowest among departments.

candidates.title: Departamento Central — core metropolitan periphery
candidates.description: Department surrounding Asunción. Intermediate-to-low poverty and the largest absolute urban population mass outside the capital.
candidates.notes: Completes the greater Asunción statistical geography. 2025 poverty ~9.9% — among the lowest.

candidates.title: Departamento de Concepción — highest-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Northern department with among the highest poverty incidence in the 2024–2025 departmental results.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 total poverty ~28.7%; frequently ranks at or near the top of the departmental poverty ranking.

candidates.title: Departamento de San Pedro — high-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Northern/interior department with elevated poverty incidence. Completes the high-poverty northern set.
candidates.notes: 2025 total poverty ~24.8%. Frequently cited alongside Concepción and Caazapá among the highest-poverty departments; also features heavily in district-level poverty maps.

candidates.title: Departamento de Caazapá — high-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Southern-interior department with elevated poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: 2025 total poverty ~25.1%. Completes the high-poverty departmental set.

candidates.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INE)
candidates.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Concepción, Caazapá, San Pedro highest; Asunción and Central lowest. National total poverty fell to ~16.0%.

candidates.title: MERCOSUR (ACE 18) — marco comercial
candidates.description: Southern Common Market customs-union and trade framework of which Paraguay is a founding member. Core preferential-trade arrangement with Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay.
referenced_by: Official trade reporting with MERCOSUR partners
candidates.notes: Foundational regional instrument. Continuously cited in Paraguayan trade and integration analysis. Brazil is the dominant bilateral partner within the bloc.

candidates.title: Acuerdo MERCOSUR–Unión Europea
candidates.description: Trade agreement between MERCOSUR and the European Union. Interim trade agreement signed in Asunción in January 2026; major preferential-access instrument for Paraguayan agro-exports.
candidates.notes: Landmark external agreement. Continuously cited as a major opening for beef, soy and other agro-products into the EU market. Signed in Asunción.

candidates.title: Presupuesto General de la Nación / National Budget
candidates.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax and other revenues (including energy royalties) with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

candidates.title: Gasto público en educación y salud
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / MEC / MSPyBS
candidates.description: Public expenditure on education and health as reflected in the national budget and related functional statistics. Complements household-survey education and health modules.
candidates.notes: Education and health are major functional allocations (education often the largest single share of the budget). Continuously tracked in budget execution and social-policy analysis; health coverage gaps remain a recurring policy issue.

proposed_edges.basis: Departmental poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national monetary-poverty measurement.
Asunción is a primary geographic domain of the EPHC.
Central forms the principal demographic and economic periphery of the greater Asunción region.
Concepción’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
MERCOSUR preferential trade is a recurring analytical dimension of merchandise-trade reporting.
The EU agreement underpins preferential access for major agro-exports.
Education and health are major functional allocations in the national budget.
